content.text:
View A represents: an upper object that is very likely blue and probably square; a right object that is very likely green and triangular; a lower object that is yellow and circular; a left object with no identified color or shape (flat distributions). Attention is currently concentrated on the lower (yellow circle), which is the most available now and remains the most recoverable after one and two steps; the other locations are much less available, with left being the least. Predicted command effects in A are locally specific: directing to a location predicts attention to stay at that location, so the system can reliably redirect from the current lower item to any other individual location.

View B represents: an upper red square, a right yellow circle, a lower blue triangle, and a left green cross. Attention is currently concentrated on the lower (blue triangle), which is highly available now and over steps; upper and left are moderately recoverable; right is less so. Predicted commands in B overwhelmingly drive selection to the right, so commands have limited control to select alternatives.
